answer: One workable design: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because velvet only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, hollow is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any trellis approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
